Synthetic land use with a known change process

Source: R/synthetic_landscape.R
synthetic_landscape.Rd

Simulates a square landscape and its land use over several periods, driven by a stated change process. It is meant for tutorials, examples and tests: unlike real data or random noise, the change has a signal a model can learn, and the process that generated it is known.

There are four classes: 1 forest, 2 arable land, 3 urban areas, 4 a lake that never changes. Two latent drivers shape both the initial map and its change:

  • accessibility, high towards the west and south, plus a smooth random field;

  • site_quality, high towards the north and east, plus a smooth random field.

In the initial map, urban land clusters where accessibility is high, the lake sits in a random patch, arable land takes the better sites and forest the rest. Each later period applies four transitions, whose per-period probabilities depend on the drivers and on the share of each class in the 5 x 5 cell neighbourhood:

transitionlogit of the per-period probability
arable -> urban-5.5 + 7 * share_urban + 3 * accessibility
forest -> urban-7 + 6 * share_urban + 3 * accessibility
forest -> arable-5 + 4 * site_quality + 3 * share_arable
arable -> forest-6 + 4 * (1 - site_quality) * (1 - accessibility) + 3 * share_forest

A cell undergoes at most one transition per period; the transitions are drawn in the order of the table. A third, random_nuisance field has no influence on the change; it is returned as a predictor a model should learn to ignore.

Arable land, with its higher economic input and output, is cleared on good sites and abandoned to forest on poor, remote ones. All random draws go through R's random number generator, so set.seed() makes a landscape reproducible.

The grid lies at the origin of Web Mercator (EPSG:3857) by default: a coordinate system that belongs to no country, with coordinates that start near zero and, at the equator, units of true metres.

Usage

synthetic_landscape(
  n_periods = 3L,
  n_cells = 30L,
  resolution = 100,
  xmin = 0,
  ymin = 0,
  crs = "EPSG:3857"
)

Arguments

n_periods

Integer, the number of maps: the initial map and n_periods - 1 steps of the process.

n_cells

Integer, cells per side of the square grid.

resolution

Numeric, cell size in the units of crs.

xmin, ymin

Numeric, the grid's lower left corner in the units of crs.

crs

Character, the grid's coordinate reference system, passed to terra::rast()

Value

A list of two terra::SpatRasters on the same grid:

  • lulc: one layer per period, named id_period=1, id_period=2, ..., holding the class of each cell;

  • drivers: the layers accessibility, site_quality and random_nuisance, in [0, 1].

Examples

set.seed(1)
landscape <- synthetic_landscape(n_periods = 3, n_cells = 30)
terra::plot(landscape$lulc, nc = 3)

terra::plot(landscape$drivers, nc = 3)
